cardTexts.card-trade-setup: 🎯 Trade Setup ⚙ LEVELS ◇ YOUR CALL The pullback plan: wait for a dip to support, then buy. Plain arithmetic, not a tested system. Pullback plan wait for a dip to support 0.3 : 1 reward : risk BUY $276.47 CLOSE $262.68 $281.07 Buy $276.47 support, 2.2% below the last close Stop $262.68 −5.0% from the buy · 2 ATR below Target $281.07 +1.7% from the buy · nearest resistance Risk $13.79 to make $4.60 a share. Size this plan → Common rules of thumb, for reference: most traders want the reward to be at least 2× the risk, and won't let a stop sit more than 7–8% below their buy (O'Neil). This card doesn't judge; you do. How this setup was formed Levels: support and resistance are zones where price turned before (swing highs and lows over the last year). The buy is the top of the nearest support zone and the target is the bottom of the nearest resistance zone above the last close. Buy and stop: buy at the nearest support, stop 2 ATR below it (ATR is how much the stock normally moves in a day). Buying a pullback near support is the canon low-risk entry (Minervini, Livermore's pivots); stops below support with an ATR buffer follow the Turtles. Zones on the bar: the faint green band is the nearest support zone and the red band the nearest resistance zone, drawn on the same price scale. A zone outside the bar's range isn't drawn; its row below still lists it. At a high with no resistance above there is no target. STA doesn't invent one. Why there is no "buy now" plan: STA's momentum system failed every backtest and the forward test, so the card doesn't show it. The pullback plan hasn't been tested by STA either; it's shown because it matches how the one tested edge works (the Mean-Reversion signal buys dips inside an uptrend). Price is Close to both support and resistance Resistance $281.07 – $282.01 · 0.8% above · turned here 2× Support $274.90 – $276.47 · 0.9% below · turned here 3× Zones are where price turned before (swing highs and lows over the last year). "Turned here N×" is how many times. The last 5 trading days can't be confirmed yet. Common trader rules, not tested.

cardTexts.card-fundamentals: 🏢 Fundamentals ◇ INFO Is the business behind the stock in trouble? Facts, not a score. No red flags 2 of 3 checks ran; none tripped. – Sales no data not checked ✓ Return on equity ROE 19.6% flag if below 0% ✓ Debt D/E 0.55 flag if above 2.0 · weaker signal for banks, utilities, REITs Next earnings · 2027-01-26 · in 70 days. If you'll still hold on that date, the price can jump either way on the report. Source: Finnhub (ROE, debt). These numbers come from a live feed and can differ from other sources (the sales growth figure most), so this card only flags clear facts and never scores. The three cutoffs haven't been backtested. How these checks were chosen Sales falling 10% or more: fast-shrinking sales are a real risk over a multi-week hold, even with a clean chart (traders who buy growth, like O'Neil, look for growing businesses). Depending on the source, the number is the latest quarter vs a year ago or the last fiscal year. Negative return on equity: the feed's return on equity is below zero, which usually means net income was negative. A plain fact. Companies with negative equity (some heavy buyback names) can show a negative ROE even when profitable. Debt/Equity above 2.0: heavy borrowing. Banks, utilities and REITs carry high debt by design, so a flag on those is weaker. Next earnings: O'Neil and Minervini avoid holding a fresh swing trade through a report, because the price can gap far past any stop. Highlighted within the app's 7-day earnings warning window. Left out on purpose: earnings growth (O'Neil's "C"): STA's field is a year-over-year rate that swings wildly when last year's earnings were tiny, so it misleads as a red flag (Day 119). P/E: a normal P/E differs a lot by sector (a bank near 10, software near 40), and it doesn't predict a 2-week move. P/E is on the Value tab.

cardTexts.card-mr-read: 🔄 Mean-Reversion Read ⚙ FORWARD-TESTED A separate question: is this a short, sharp dip worth buying for a bounce? No signal Blocked by: the 2-day RSI is 10 or higher. Buying the dip needs all four to pass Has it dropped hard over the last 2 days? ✗ 2-day RSI 39.3 needs under 10 (a very sharp drop) sharp drop sharp rise RSI(2) scores recent momentum from 0 to 100, weighted mostly to the last 2 days. Low = it just fell fast. High = it just rose fast. Is it in an uptrend? ✓ 13.0% above its 200-day average needs to be above it below above The 200-day average is the usual line between an uptrend and a downtrend. Is the price high enough? ✓ $282.55 needs above $10 This skips penny stocks. Does it trade enough to get in and out? ✓ $2B traded on an average day needs above $25M Average of the last 20 days. Enough trading means you can get in and out. Checked on the 2026-11-16 close; today's bar is still forming, and the system only decides on completed days. How this read was formed What it is: Larry Connors' RSI(2) system ("Short Term Trading Strategies That Work"). RSI(2) scores recent momentum from 0 to 100, weighted mostly to the last 2 days; below 10 means a sharp, short drop. It buys that drop only while the stock is above its 200-day average, so it doesn't buy a falling knife. The four rules: the 2-day RSI below 10, close above the 200-day average, price above $10, and average daily trading above $25M (so you can get in and out cleanly). All four must pass. Track record: the rules were tested across many stocks with fills at the next open (what you can actually do). That record is about the system, not this stock. Independent of the Technical Read: a stock can pass most trend checks there and show No signal here, or the other way round. They answer different questions, and neither gates the other.

What these numbers are The three tiles are common rules of thumb: at least 7 of 8 trend checks pass, RSI is between 50 and 70 (rising but not overheated), and the stock has done better than the S&P 500 over the past year. STA has not tested them, and they do not predict what happens next. They describe the stock; the decision is yours. Why only 4 checks are listed: the full score uses 8 checks from Mark Minervini's Trend Template. The 4 listed are the ones most traders lean on; the other 4 mostly repeat them. Trend strength (ADX): ADX measures how hard the price is pushing in one direction. Below 20 means it's moving sideways right now. In an uptrend that usually means resting, not a broken trend. Prices are adjusted for dividends: older prices (and so highs and averages) are lowered for dividends paid, so for a dividend payer they can sit a little below what the chart showed on the day. The 1-year high here and on the Price Data card are the same number. Slow vs fast averages: the trend checks use simple averages, which don't flip on a few noisy days. The price gauge uses a fast (exponential) 21-day average. Stops use neither; they're based on ATR. The price gauge and ladder show where the price sits against its 21, 50 and 200-day averages: the gauge in day-moves, the ladder in real dollars. It follows an old trading idea: buying far above the 21-day average means a farther stop (Livermore's pivotal points, O'Neil's "don't buy extended"). It shows for every stock and only measures; when to buy is your call.
